passage: The Tanaka group compared two receptor proteins, A and B, that bind a steroid ligand with different affinities. Purified protein was held at 1 nM, a concentration far below either dissociation constant, so that the free ligand concentration was approximately equal to the total added. Ligand was titrated over a wide range, and the fraction of protein with bound ligand was measured by fluorescence anisotropy after each addition reached equilibrium. Each binding curve was hyperbolic and showed no evidence of cooperativity. The researchers intend to use the receptor with the tighter binding as a biosensor, and they want to know what ligand concentration would be required to saturate it at 80% occupancy. All measurements were made at 25 °C in identical buffer. Protein stocks were centrifuged before use to remove aggregates, and ligand stocks were verified by absorbance. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: At [ligand] = 100 nM, what is the fraction of protein A bound?
questions.explanation: Fraction bound = [L]/(Kd + [L]) = 100/(20+100) = 0.83. The B column gives 0.33.
questions.trap: Reading 0.91 (protein A at 200 nM) or 0.33 (protein B at 100 nM) instead of protein A at 100 nM.

questions.stem: Why was protein held far below the Kd?

options.A: So that cooperativity can be detected
options.B: So that the protein is certain to be fully saturated
options.C: So that ligand depletion by binding is negligible and free ligand ≈ total ligand
options.D: So that Kd equals the protein concentration

questions.explanation: If protein were comparable to Kd, binding would deplete free ligand and distort the fit to the simple hyperbola.
questions.trap: Thinking the low protein concentration is meant to detect cooperativity or saturate the protein; its purpose is to keep free ligand equal to total ligand.

questions.stem: What ligand concentration is needed for 80% occupancy of the higher-affinity protein (Kd = 20 nM)?
questions.trap: Using 2 x Kd (40 nM) or mixing up 80% with 50% occupancy; at 80% occupancy [L] = 4 x Kd.

options.A: A hyperbolic curve is consistent with noncooperative binding
options.B: Protein A binds the ligand with higher affinity than protein B
options.C: A lower Kd means lower affinity
options.D: Kd equals the ligand concentration at half-saturation

questions.explanation: Kd is inversely related to affinity: a smaller Kd means tighter binding.
questions.trap: Equating a lower Kd with weaker binding; a smaller Kd means tighter binding (higher affinity).

questions.stem: Which protein behavior differs from these hyperbolic curves?

options.B: Hemoglobin's sigmoidal oxygen binding due to cooperativity
options.C: Binding of a single ligand to one site on a monomeric protein

questions.explanation: Hemoglobin binds O₂ cooperatively (Hill coefficient > 1), giving a sigmoidal curve, while myoglobin is hyperbolic like proteins A and B.
questions.trap: Picking myoglobin or Michaelis-Menten saturation as different from proteins A and B; both are hyperbolic, and only cooperative hemoglobin is sigmoidal.
